name: dbt OSS (dbt Core)
sku: dbt OSS 2.0: the Apache 2.0 build of the v2 Rust engine (`dbt-oss`, called dbt Core 2.0 until the rename). It has the dbt project language, the standard commands, dbt Docs v2 and dbt State, and lacks what only the free proprietary dbt (v2) adds: SQL comprehension and static analysis, the language server, `dbt lint` and the VS Code extension, which are scored in dbt-v2-additions. The v2 engine lists BigQuery, Databricks, Redshift, Snowflake and DuckDB (CLI) as GA, Spark as beta and ClickHouse as private beta; PostgreSQL is not listed, so a Postgres project still needs dbt v1 (Python, final minor 1.13, still patched), which is not scored here. Scores come from docs.getdbt.com pages that describe the framework in general. The v2 upgrade guide says nearly all v1 capability carries over, but Python models, MetricFlow and state selection were not individually confirmed for v2.

transform.sql-transform.note: The reason the product exists: models are SQL SELECT statements that dbt compiles, orders and materialises in the warehouse.

transform.code-transform.note: Python models run remotely on Snowflake (Snowpark), BigQuery or Databricks, not locally. Only some adapters support them, and only table and incremental materialisations.

orchestrate.dependency-dag.note: ref() calls build the dependency graph automatically so models deploy in the right order. It orders dbt's own nodes only; it is not a general task DAG.

orchestrate.ci-cd.note: state:modified selection plus --defer enable slim CI, running only changed models and their dependents. dbt supplies the comparison logic; a separate runner still has to execute it.

serve.semantic-layer.note: Metrics and semantic models are defined in YAML (MetricFlow, Apache 2.0) and can be queried from the CLI. The Semantic Layer API and BI integrations need the dbt platform.

bands.note: Generic tests (unique, not_null, accepted_values, relationships), singular SQL tests and unit tests ship in the box and run as part of the build.
Tests can also be declared on sources and run against raw tables (dbt test --select source:*), but only after the data has landed. Nothing is checked in flight.

Model contracts fix column names, types and constraints, and the build fails if the output drifts. How much the warehouse enforces varies: Postgres enforces most constraints, Snowflake and Redshift enforce only not_null.
Not part of dbt. Elementary's Apache-2.0 dbt package adds volume, freshness and column-distribution anomaly tests, and is maintained by a separate company.

The docs site includes a DAG of the project, which dbt Docs v2 also shows. It is model-level and covers dbt-managed nodes only. Column-level lineage needs strict static analysis, which is in the dbt (v2) distribution behind a free login, so it is scored in dbt-v2-additions.

dbt docs generate builds a static, searchable site of models, sources, descriptions and column metadata that can be hosted anywhere. It covers dbt assets only; the richer Catalog is a paid platform feature.
The grants config makes dbt issue grant and revoke statements so each model's permissions match configuration. Supported on adapters including Snowflake, Databricks, Redshift and BigQuery.
A profile holds multiple targets, typically dev and prod, selected per command with --target.

presentation.tagline: Apache 2.0 SQL-first transformation framework: models, tests and docs kept in version control.
